author: Sarojini Naidu
title: The Golden Threshold
edition: London: William Heinemann, 1905. Scan-backed Wikisource transcription, The Golden Threshold.djvu; individual poem subpages preserve stanza and line boundaries. HTML emphasis/small caps are flattened without altering words; nonbreaking spaces become spaces, indentation and trailing layout whitespace are normalized. The Wikisource pages are proofread once (level 3) except Palanquin-Bearers (validated), so all eight poems first selected were collated line by line, including punctuation, with the 1905 page images (pp. 27–32, 39, 44–45, 49, 53). Five transcription errors are corrected to the print: Indian Weavers “solemn and still,” (p. 30); Coromandel Fishers “pray to the morning light,” (p. 31); In Praise of Henna “afloat on the tide,” “ere the dawn be old,” and “fingers and feet,” (p. 39). The other poems match the print; Cradle-Song and Alabaster, which also match, are no longer in the sequence. Selected poems were composed in English, not translated. The library text holds the dedication and every poem in the book; Arthur Symons’s introduction is not included. On 2026-11-18 twelve more poems were collated line by line, punctuation included, with the page images of the same scan (Internet Archive goldenthreshold00naidgoog, from which the djvu was made; pp. 33–38, 40–42, 63–64, 77–81, 83–86, 90–96): The Snake-Charmer, Corn-Grinders, Village-Song, Harvest Hymn, In the Forest, The Queen’s Rival, The Indian Gipsy, To My Children, Nightfall in the City of Hyderabad, Street Cries, To India and The Royal Tombs of Golconda. Sixteen readings are corrected to the print, most of them commas the transcription had dropped or set as full stops: “loiter, by”, “laugh in the sky” (the transcription had “shy”), “I am going,” and “lilies glisten,”, “our sowing,” and “all blessing, we hail thee,”, “murmuring rose:” and “silken thread,”, “agile grace,”, “unclouded morn,”, “the muezzin’s call”, “winding lanes,” and “comes majestical,”, “koïls”, “the spheres,” and “dost thou sleep?”; and the row of five points printed in The Queen’s Rival after “Seven handmaids meet for the Persian Queen.” is restored as its own paragraph. Since the unchecked poems are likely to hold similar errors, scope.collated lists the poems collated so far, these and the eight collated earlier.

rights.basis: The original English text in this 1905 edition was published before 1931 and is public domain in the United States in 2026. The dated source and its public-domain record are linked; no modern introductions, annotations, or illustrations are reproduced.

acquisition.method: Whole library text: every page of the scan-backed Wikisource transcription (Index: The Golden Threshold.djvu, pages 1–108) rendered in one MediaWiki API request that transcludes them in order (the download URL; sent as a POST with the same parameters), converted by a scratch Node script. Kept Naidu’s dedication to Edmund Gosse (with its London, 1896 / Hyderabad, 1905 lines, as one stanza) and the three sections Folk Songs, Songs for Music and Poems with every poem; excluded the publisher’s advertisements, title and copyright pages, the contents, and Arthur Symons’s introduction, which is not the author’s. Section names and poem titles are headings, the parenthetical subtitles one-line paragraphs; each stanza keeps its lines without indentation; inline emphasis, small capitals and the transcription’s tooltip notes are flattened. The five corrections to the print declared in the edition statement are made (solemn and still, pray to the morning light, afloat on the tide, ere the dawn be old, fingers and feet). Every nightly reading was located exactly. The sixteen corrections of the 2026-11-18 collation and the restored row of points are then applied (see the edition statement).
